title: Introduction to the Seerah and the Era of Jahiliyyah
overview: This lecture introduces the spiritual and practical benefits of studying the Seerah of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, emphasizing its role in understanding the Quran and increasing faith. The speaker explores the ancient history of Makkah, from the settlement of Ibrahim and Ismail to the eventual corruption of pure monotheism into the idol worship of the Jahiliyyah period.
chapters: Benefits of Studying the Seerah
Understanding Revelation through Context
The Foundations of Meccan Civilization
Rebuilding the Ka'bah and the Call to Hajj
The Corruption of Tawhid and Introduction of Shirk
The Moral Decline of Jahiliyyah

title: Judaism in Yemen and the History of the Kiswah
overview: This episode explores the historical introduction of Judaism and Christianity into the Arabian Peninsula, focusing on the conversion of the Yemeni king Tibban As'ad. It details the prophecy of the Prophet's ﷺ migration to Madinah and the origin of the Kiswah covering the Ka'bah.
chapters: Introduction and Religious Context
Rabiah ibn Nasr and the Dream of Conquest
The Siege of Yathrib and a King's Change of Heart
The Prophecy of the Promised Land
The Treachery of Hudhayl and Respect for the Ka'bah
The First Kiswah and the Trial by Fire

title: The Fall of the Tubba and the Rise of Christianity in Najran
overview: This episode explores the internal collapse of the Tubba dynasty in Yemen due to arrogance and betrayal, leading to a period of political chaos. It further details the miraculous introduction of Unitarian Christianity to Najran by the pious slave Faymiyun, completing the religious landscape of the Arabian Peninsula before the birth of the Prophet ﷺ.
chapters: The Arrogance of Hassan ibn Tibban As'ad
The Assassination Plot
The Guilt of King Amr
Civil War and the Rule of Lakhni'ah
Dhu Nuwas and the Restoration
The Entry of Christianity into Najran
Conclusion: The Religious Map of Arabia

title: The Boy and the King: The Martyrs of the Trench
overview: This episode recounts the spread of Christianity in Yemen through the miraculous story of a young boy who chose faith over sorcery. It details the brutal martyrdom of twenty thousand believers in the 'trench of fire' and the subsequent conquest of Yemen by the Abyssinian army led by Abrahah.
chapters: Christianity's Entry into Najran
The Boy, the Monk, and the Sorcerer
Miracles and the Proof of Truth
The Failed Executions
The Supreme Sacrifice of the Ghulam
The People of the Trench
The Abyssinian Conquest of Yemen

title: The Year of the Elephant and the Divine Protection of the Ka'bah
overview: This episode details the historical events leading to the attempted destruction of the Ka'bah by the Abyssinian governor Abrahah. It covers the political shifts in Yemen, the rivalry between the church of al-Qulays and the Ka'bah, and the miraculous intervention of Allah in the Year of the Elephant, which coincided with the birth of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
chapters: The Abyssinian Conquest of Yemen
The Rise of Abrahah al-Ashram
Al-Qulays and the Provocation of Ahl al-Nasi'
The March on Makkah and the Treachery of Thaqif
The Meeting of Abdul Muttalib and Abrahah
The Miraculous Destruction of the Army

title: The Persian Conquest of Yemen and the Conversion of Badhan
overview: This episode details the transition of Yemen from Ethiopian to Persian control following the efforts of Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan to reclaim his ancestral land. It highlights the miraculous events surrounding the Prophet Muhammad's ‷ letter to the Persian Emperor Kisra and the subsequent conversion of the Persian governor Badhan to Islam.

Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan Seeks an Ally

The Ruse of the Mountains of Gold
The Battle for Yemen
The Prediction of Kisra's Death
Guidance and the Hearts of Men

title: Qusayy ibn Kilab and the Rise of the Quraysh
overview: This lecture returns to the history of Makkah to explain how the descendants of Ismail reclaimed leadership of the city. It details the rise of Qusayy ibn Kilab, the establishment of the council hall Dar al-Nadwah, and the lineage leading to the Prophet's grandfather, Abdul Muttalib.
